title: Python: A2, module.Class.method resolves (m.C.st() and m.C.meth(m.C()) are unresolved on dev)
description: DEC-303 (a22) item 3 admitted group A2, module.Class.method; (a45) item 1: A2 has no task id, and a lookup on dev 6f1dd89 (read-only, 2026-11-26) shows it MISSING. Reproduction: m.py class C with def meth(self) and a @staticmethod def st(); app.py: import m; m.C.st(); m.C().meth(); m.C.meth(m.C()). Result on dev: m.C() resolves (the construction) and m.C().meth() resolves, but m.C.st() and m.C.meth(m.C()) draw no edge to the method (name bin, nothing resolved). The Cls.attr lookup exists for a bare class name (ALIAS and the A2-lookup comment in test/python-calls.test.ts near the ALIAS describe) but not through a module attribute chain. A defect against rules in force, no new rule: fix and fixtures as for the other admitted groups, red/green with callee-symbol pinning and the full bin delta, positive twins, the five-pin corpus diff per (a34) and (a40) item 2 with every in-repo edge created or removed reported before the clear. Built AFTER GCLI-116 lands and before the analyzer freezes; joins the (a36) item 1(i) hold list as an (a22) group (opum-doc to confirm).
